tells: 1. The laugh barely builds over 1 s. Only the white-shirt woman lifts her hand to her mouth (t=12.6 to 13.0). Green hoodie, purple top and grey-jacket blonde hold nearly the same pose, so the beat doesn't read as caused by a line (club-5-strip.png, centre and right of every frame)
2. Rocketbox game-era faces: waxy, evenly lit skin with no subsurface and painted-looking eyes. In close-up it reads as a 2010s cutscene, not a person (club-4-face.png, centre face)
3. The background blonde's head and neck sit at a broken angle over her shoulder, as if detached or twisted, and the soft defocus makes it worse (club-4-face.png, left third)

4. The bar backlight is a flat, blown rectangle with a hard clipped hotspot and a cardboard silhouette standing in front. It is the brightest thing in frame and pulls the eye off the audience (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper centre / upper left)

5. Practicals are cloned: every wall sconce is the same blown trapezoid, and every candle cup glows the same flat pink with no flicker variation. The front faces are lit by an unmotivated soft frontal key rather than the candles below them (club-1-wide.png, walls and table tops)

1. The rows behind are flat dark cut-out impostors: identical cardboard heads and shoulders with no volume or seat depth. They read as a painted backdrop, not a full house (theatre-1-wide.png, upper half; theatre-2-mid.png, top right)

2. The rake is wrong: the second row appears to stand or float, with whole torsos visible above the front row's heads, and an isolated lit figure stands in the dark left aisle (theatre-1-wide.png, centre rows and far left)

3. Two front rows sit in a hard spot pool and everything behind falls off a cliff to black. There is no stage spill gradient, no contact shadows on seats or knees, and the lit people look pasted onto the dark (theatre-1-wide.png, theatre-3-mid.png, front rows)

4. The face close mid-laugh reads as a yawn: glassy fixed eyes, a mouth opened without the cheeks or eyes engaging, and blocky low-poly red seat boxes in the defocus (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and bottom corners)
5. Cut-off low-poly people at the frame edge: a slab-white sleeve and faceted shoulders, and geometry clipping in the seats on the left (theatre-6-held.png, left third)
1. The wide's front row is posed like a class photo: everyone square to camera, hands on knees almost symmetrically, little lean or slump variation (openmic-1-wide.png, front row)

2. Hair alpha dithering and stipple on the yellow-shirt man's hair edge, plus a floating disembodied hand on the blurred blonde's chest (openmic-4-face.png, top right of the head and right background)

3. Laugh mouths open to a dark, flat interior with uniform teeth, and the eyes don't squint with the laugh, so the joy reads as a mask (openmic-2-mid.png, green-shirt woman and brown-hair woman, centre right)

4. The room is a black void above the downlights, and the bright flat door panel on the left wall is unmotivated. It looks like an untextured box, not a lit doorway (openmic-1-wide.png, top 25% and upper left)

5. Arm interpenetration as neighbours touch during the laugh: the green-shirt woman's forearm passes into the hoodie woman's arm and torso (openmic-5-strip.png, t=13.0 frame centre right; openmic-2-mid.png, centre)
